bib.title: DoRA: Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Vienna, PMLR 235

question: Why does LoRA trail full fine-tuning in accuracy, and can a magnitude/direction reparameterisation close the gap without added inference cost?
hypothesis: A negative correlation between magnitude and direction updates (as in FT) is more optimal than LoRA's positive one; letting LoRA handle only the direction while training magnitude separately gives FT-like learning capacity.
contributions: DoRA, a PEFT method that decomposes pretrained weight into magnitude and direction, training magnitude directly and direction with LoRA, with no extra inference latency
A weight decomposition analysis showing different learning patterns of FT and LoRA
DoRA consistently surpasses LoRA across NLP and vision-language tasks and backbones (LLM and LVLM)

method.summary: Weight W0 is split as m*V/||V||_c with m=||W0||_c (trainable vector, 1 x k) and V=W0 frozen plus low-rank BA update, W'=m (W0+BA)/||W0+BA||_c. The column norm is detached from the gradient graph to save memory. Compared against LoRA, adapters and prefix on LLaMA family, VL-BART and LLaVA-1.5-7B.
method.task: parameter-efficient fine-tuning (commonsense reasoning, image/video-text understanding, visual instruction tuning, instruction tuning)

datasets.name: Merged training sets of 8 commonsense tasks (BoolQ, PIQA, SIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-e, ARC-c, OBQA)
datasets.split: training sets of all 8 tasks merged; each task's test set evaluated separately

datasets.name: LLaVA-1.5 visual instruction tuning data
datasets.preprocessing: training data filter and prompt format follow LLaVA-1.5

models.name: DoRA
models.init_from: m=||W0||_c, V=W0, B=0, A Kaiming uniform

models.name: LoRA, Prefix, Series adapter, Parallel adapter, FT, VeRA

training.lr: commonsense: LLaMA-7B 2e-4 (r16)/1e-4 (r32); LLaMA-13B 3e-4/2e-4; LLaMA2-7B 2e-4/2e-4; LLaMA3-8B 1e-4/1e-4; VL-BART 1e-3 image-text, 3e-4 video-text; LLaVA 2e-4; Alpaca DoRA 4e-4, DVoRA 4e-3

other.rank_alpha: commonsense: DoRA† r=16 alpha=32, DoRA r=32 alpha=64 (Table 8 lists both columns per model; pairing is read from the column order). VL-BART r=128 alpha=128; LLaVA r=128 alpha=256; Alpaca DoRA r=64, DVoRA r=1024
other.target_modules: commonsense Q,K,V,Up,Down; VL-BART Q,K; LLaVA and Alpaca Q,K,V,O,Up,Down,Gate
other.hp_selection: DoRA is fine-tuned following the LoRA configuration with same rank, adjusting only the learning rate (commonsense); LoRA on LLaMA/LLaMA-13B and other baselines copied from Hu et al. 2023; LoRA on LLaMA2-7B and LLaMA3-8B run with Hu et al. hyperparameters (not re-tuned); LLaVA and VL-BART and VeRA/Alpaca use the baseline's own published config. The paper does not say how the DoRA learning rate was searched (grid, validation set, number of trials).
other.memory: GPU memory: LLaMA-7B 37.3 GB -> 28.2 GB with detached norm; VL-BART 23.4 -> 20.5 GB; GPU type not stated

inference.samples: inferred: single run per cell; no seeds or variance reported
inference.prompting: commonsense: ChatGPT baseline zero-shot CoT; fine-tuned models per Hu et al. 2023

metrics.name: MT-Bench score
metrics.definition: GPT-4 scores each answer out of 10, averaged

metrics.name: delta M / delta D
metrics.definition: mean over columns of |m_FT - m_0| and of 1 - cos(V_FT^n, W0^n)

eval.protocol: Single reported number per cell; no seeds, no significance test; baseline numbers partly copied from earlier papers.

evidence.quote: we initially fine-tuned models with DoRA following the LoRA configuration, maintaining the same rank while adjusting only the learning rate

results.claim: On VL-BART query matrices, the correlation between direction change and magnitude change is -0.62 for FT, -0.31 for DoRA and +0.83 for LoRA.
results.metric: correlation of delta D and delta M
results.setup: Weight decomposition analysis on VL-BART fine-tuned on four image-text tasks, LoRA/DoRA on query and value matrices (query analysed in Fig 2), single run, checkpoints at three intermediate steps and final; pairs of (delta D, delta M) across layers and steps
results.quote: both FT and DoRA exhibit negative correlation values of -0.62 and -0.31, respectively. In contrast, LoRA shows a positive correlation with a value of 0.83

results.claim: LLaMA-7B commonsense average: LoRA 74.7, DoRA 78.4, DoRA† (half rank) 77.5.
results.setup: Commonsense reasoning: 8 tasks, training sets merged, per-task test; LLaMA-7B, rank 32 for LoRA and DoRA (DoRA† rank 16); LoRA/baselines on LLaMA-7B/13B copied from Hu et al. 2023, LoRA on LLaMA2-7B and LLaMA3-8B run by the authors with Hu et al. hyperparameters; avg of 8 accuracies
results.table: Table 1, LLaMA-7B rows LoRA 74.7, DoRA† (Ours) 77.5, DoRA (Ours) 78.4, column Avg.

results.claim: DoRA† with half the LoRA rank still beats LoRA on all four backbones.
results.setup: Commonsense reasoning: 8 tasks, training sets merged, per-task test; LLaMA-7B, rank 32 for LoRA and DoRA (DoRA† rank 16); LoRA/baselines on LLaMA-7B/13B copied from Hu et al. 2023, LoRA on LLaMA2-7B and LLaMA3-8B run by the authors with Hu et al. hyperparameters; avg of 8 accuracies; LLaMA-7B / 13B / LLaMA2-7B / LLaMA3-8B
results.quote: DoRA† exceeds LoRA’s performance on LLaMA-7B by 2.8%, on LLaMA-13B by 1%, on LLaMA2-7B by 2.9%, and on LLaMA3-8B by 4.2%, despite having only half as many trainable parameters as LoRA

results.claim: DoRA adds only about 0.01% trainable parameters over LoRA at the same rank (learnable magnitude vector of size 1 x k); e.g. LLaMA-7B 0.83% vs 0.84%.
results.setup: Commonsense reasoning: 8 tasks, training sets merged, per-task test; LLaMA-7B, rank 32 for LoRA and DoRA (DoRA† rank 16); LoRA/baselines on LLaMA-7B/13B copied from Hu et al. 2023, LoRA on LLaMA2-7B and LLaMA3-8B run by the authors with Hu et al. hyperparameters; avg of 8 accuracies
results.quote: The marginal increase of 0.01% in the number of trainable parameters for DoRA over LoRA, as detailed in Table 1, arises from the inclusion of learnable magnitude components (parameter of size 1 × k)

results.claim: DoRA with LLaMA-7B reaches 78.4 against ChatGPT zero-shot CoT 77.0 on the commonsense average.
results.setup: Commonsense reasoning: 8 tasks, training sets merged, per-task test; LLaMA-7B, rank 32 for LoRA and DoRA (DoRA† rank 16); LoRA/baselines on LLaMA-7B/13B copied from Hu et al. 2023, LoRA on LLaMA2-7B and LLaMA3-8B run by the authors with Hu et al. hyperparameters; avg of 8 accuracies; ChatGPT = gpt-3.5-turbo zero-shot CoT
results.table: Table 1, row ChatGPT column Avg. 77.0; LLaMA-7B DoRA Avg. 78.4

results.claim: At rank 8 LoRA collapses to 40.74% average while DoRA keeps 77.96%.
results.setup: LLaMA-7B, commonsense reasoning, ranks {4,8,16,32,64}, Table 15 / Fig 5; avg of 8 accuracies
results.quote: LoRA’s average accuracies drop to 40.74% for r = 8 and 39.49% for r = 4. In contrast, DoRA retains a notable accuracy of 77.96% for r = 8 and 61.89% for r = 4

results.claim: At rank 4 LoRA averages 39.49% and DoRA 61.89%.
results.setup: LLaMA-7B, commonsense reasoning, ranks {4,8,16,32,64}, Table 15 / Fig 5; avg of 8 accuracies
results.quote: LoRA’s average accuracies drop to 40.74% for r = 8 and 39.49% for r = 4. In contrast, DoRA retains a notable accuracy of 77.96% for r = 8 and 61.89% for r = 4

results.claim: At rank 64 both degrade: LoRA 65.8, DoRA 72.1 (HellaSwag collapses to 17.6 for LoRA, 40.7 for DoRA); best LoRA is rank 32 (74.7), best DoRA rank 32 (78.4).
results.setup: LLaMA-7B, commonsense reasoning, ranks {4,8,16,32,64}, Table 15 / Fig 5; avg of 8 accuracies
results.note: Authors do not comment on the rank-64 drop or the single-task collapses; no seeds/variance reported, so these may be training instabilities.
results.table: Table 15, rows r=64: LoRA Avg. 65.8, DoRA Avg. 72.1

results.claim: LLaVA-1.5-7B visual instruction tuning, 7-benchmark average: FT 66.5, LoRA 66.9, DoRA 67.6.
results.setup: LLaVA-1.5-7B (Vicuna-1.5-7B + CLIP ViT-L/336px), DoRA uses the LoRA config of Liu et al. 2023a (rank 128, alpha 256, 1 epoch, lr 2e-4), 4.61% LoRA vs 4.63% DoRA params, avg over VQAv2, GQA, VisWiz, SQA, VQAT, POPE, MMBench
results.note: Intro/abstract-level text says +0.6 on LLaVA-7B; Table 4 gives 67.6-66.9 = 0.7. Per task, DoRA is below LoRA on VQAv2 (78.6 vs 79.1) and VQAT (57 vs 58.2); gain is driven by VisWiz (52.2 vs 47.8) and SQA (69.9 vs 68.4).
results.quote: DoRA still demonstrates superior performance over both LoRA and FT, with an average improvement of 0.7% over LoRA and 1.1% over FT

results.claim: Authors note LoRA already beats FT on LLaVA, so DoRA's headroom is smaller.
results.setup: LLaVA-1.5-7B
results.quote: the average accuracy of LoRA already surpasses FT, which could imply that FT might be experiencing issues with overfitting

results.claim: Detaching the weight norm ||V+dV||_c from the gradient graph cuts LLaMA-7B fine-tuning memory by 24.4% (37.3 GB to 28.2 GB) with 0.2 points lower commonsense accuracy (78.3 to 78.1).
results.setup: LLaMA-7B commonsense, DoRA, accumulation steps 4, batch size 16, GPU memory in GB per Table 7 (GPU type not stated)
results.note: Accuracy 78.3 without vs 78.1 with. VL-BART: 23.4 GB to 20.5 GB (-12.4%), accuracy 77.3 vs 77.4. All reported DoRA results use the modification.
results.quote: the modification leads to a training memory reduction of approximately 24.4% in fine-tuning LLaMA and 12.4% in VL-BART

results.claim: The detach modification costs 0.2 points on LLaMA and nothing on VL-BART.
results.setup: LLaMA-7B commonsense avg, DoRA with vs without gradient detach on the norm
results.quote: shows a negligible difference of only 0.2 compared to DoRA without the modification on LLaMA

results.claim: DoRA and DVoRA beat LoRA and VeRA at every Alpaca sample size (1000, 4000, 7000, 10000); at 1000 samples margins are 0.29 and 0.22, at 7000 samples 0.3 and 0.33.
results.setup: LLaMA2-7B MT-Bench, Fig 4 (LLaMA-7B Fig 9)
results.quote: with 7000 training samples, DoRA and DVoRA surpass LoRA and VeRA by margins of 0.3 and 0.33, respectively. Even when the sample size is reduced to 1000, DoRA and DVoRA maintain their lead with advantages of 0.29 and 0.22 over LoRA and VeRA, respectively

results.claim: Tuning granularity: updating direction+magnitude only on QKV and magnitude only on the other modules gives LLaMA-7B 77.5 (0.39% params) vs LoRA 74.7 (0.83%); LLaMA-13B 81.3 (0.31%) vs 80.5 (0.67%).
results.setup: Commonsense reasoning, Table 6
results.quote: DoRA surpasses LoRA by 2.8% on LLaMA-7B and 0.8% on LLaMA-13B, while utilizing only less than half of the trainable parameters compared to LoRA

results.claim: QDoRA beats QLoRA by 0.19 (LLaMA2-7B) and 0.23 (LLaMA3-8B) exact match on Orca-Math and slightly beats full FT; the experiment is by Answer.AI, not the authors.
results.setup: 100k Orca-Math samples, 500 held out, exact match; run by Turgutlu et al. 2024 with FSDP
results.quote: QDoRA not only significantly surpasses QLoRA by 0.19/0.23 on LLaMA2-7B and LLaMA3-8B
results.source: Kerem Turgutlu, Jonathan Whitaker, J. Howard 2024 (answer.ai FSDP QDoRA)

results.claim: DoRA moves weights less than LoRA in both magnitude and direction on LLaMA2-7B commonsense fine-tuning (Fig 3, Fig 8), which the authors read as supporting a negative delta-D/delta-M correlation being better.
results.setup: LLaMA2-7B fine-tuned on commonsense, query/key/value matrices across layers
results.quote: DoRA fine-tuned weights show less deviation from the pre-trained weights in both magnitude and direction, while the differences for the LoRA fine-tuned weights are significantly larger

limits: Weight-decomposition analysis (correlations -0.62/-0.31/0.83) is a single VL-BART case study on query/value matrices of a small model, not LLaMA; LLaMA2-7B is only shown as magnitude/direction deviation plots.
No seeds, variance or significance tests; many gains are 0.3 to 1 point and per-task numbers move both ways.
DoRA learning rate was tuned while LoRA baselines on LLaMA2-7B/LLaMA3-8B used the fixed Hu et al. 2023 hyperparameters, so the comparison is not equally tuned.
Rank-64 rows in Table 15 show collapses (HellaSwag 17.6 LoRA, 40.7 DoRA) that the authors do not discuss.
Text vs table mismatches: DoRA† vs LoRA on LLaMA-13B called +1% but table gives +0.3; LLaVA gain +0.6 in intro vs +0.7 in Sec 5.3.
Authors concede on LLaVA that LoRA already beats FT so the DoRA improvement is smaller; the explanation (FT overfitting) is not tested.
QDoRA and text-to-image results are initial, QDoRA is by third parties, SDXL results are qualitative images only.
Training compute, GPU type, sequence length, precision and seeds are not stated.
Training memory saving is measured on two setups only and wall-clock cost of DoRA vs LoRA is not reported.

grad_{V'} L = (m / C) grad_{W'} L, C = ||V'||_c
